items.q: What did Peter Ahn say when NBC asked for Dropbox's biggest customer?
items.a: The truth: **2,000 seats at National Geographic**, no Fortune 500 yet — NBC would be first. Box was marketing GE at 100k. NBC was 42,000. Lenny Bloom later: that was the right answer; he likes to be **the first patient.** First three-year multi-million. **Enterprise sales is a trust exercise.**

items.q: Who should a startup sell to?
items.a: **Innovators, not followers.** If the buyer wanted the 100k reference logo, Dropbox loses. Filter for people excited to work with an underdog. Most buyers follow.

**Value first, then ask.** Not 'want a call about sales?' — 'I wrote three mistakes salespeople make. Want it?' They research you, learn one thing, then you ask for time. Email is noisy: find the Slack / Reddit / conference where the problem is already spoken.

items.q: What is month one at a technical company?
items.a: Get to **sales-engineer depth** — docs, 'stupid' engineer/PM questions, under the hood — **before** you put points on the board. People trust experts. The job is future tech that solves a problem **today.**

sections.title: Put the stutter in the process

items.q: How did Ahn turn a stutter into a sales tool?
items.a: **Slowdown phrases** that buy thinking time: 'let me think about that'; 'I don't know the exact answer right now'; 'can we go back to the beginning?' ESL + stutter became the product. Korean BBQ / karaoke instead of the steakhouse. Personality in the deal, not Ferrari-bro costume.
